findings.issue: file_changes phase can pass with a tracking-only/evidence-only commit recorded as the implementation commit. hasCommitRecord only checks that the recorded SHA is HEAD, or HEAD^ when HEAD is a same-phase tracking commit. It never verifies that the recorded commit itself contains any non-tracking implementation file. The current positive fixture records the commit made from only evidence/reviews as phaseCommit, so the gate proves the bypass exists.
findings.recommendation: For commit_intent:"file_changes", require the accepted implementation SHA to contain at least one non-tracking artifact path, and reject any candidate whose changed files are only phase-result/evidence/reviews. Add a regression test where HEAD^ is evidence/reviews-only plus HEAD phase-result-only and assert failure; update the passing fixture to include a real implementation file commit.

findings.issue: build-code stage-result validation still allows facts.review to be omitted, while workflows/build-code/SKILL.md lines 122-128 define facts.review as a required key and the round scope says raw JSON review verdict paths are required for gate/stage facts. A build-code stage-result with changed/tests/worktree_root/task_tracking_root but no review currently passes validateStageResult.
findings.recommendation: Add "review" to build-code required_keys, add semantics for it, and add negative/positive tests in tests/facts-subschema.test.mjs requiring a non-empty facts.review object with the raw JSON artifact path contract.

resolutionSummary: Tests were rerun and passed: npm test -- tests/phase-gate.test.mjs tests/facts-subschema.test.mjs tests/verify-code-capture.test.mjs tests/receipt-verification.test.mjs (107 passed). git diff --check passed. Review still blocks because the phase gate can accept a tracking-only commit as implementation, and the build-code facts schema does not enforce the required review fact.

findings.description: Spec describes or requires eliminating internal contradictions between field contracts or rule statements (cluster A: schema/contract terms + cluster B: conflict/contradiction/duplicate terms). Multiple conflicting schemas for the same entity cause silent drift — schema-drift blocking.
